react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA (merged DB), Mummichog m/z-network activity (human_mfn), and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA — converge on steroid hormone metabolism as the dominant biological signal. RaMP ORA returned KEGG:hsa00150 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) and its SMPDB/WikiPathways/Reactome equivalents (SMPDB:SMP00068, WP:WP4523, REACT:R-HSA-196071, REACT:R-HSA-8957322) with FDR < 2.2e-14 and fold-enrichment > 1000, driven by five input steroids: testosterone (C00535/CHEBI:17347), 17β-estradiol (C00951/CHEBI:16469), androstenedione (C00280/CHEBI:16422), DHEA (C01227/CHEBI:28689), and dihydrotestosterone (C03917/CHEBI:16330). Mummichog independently identified MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism (p=0.0024) with 10/10 input steroids mapping to that network module — a perfect overlap — and the closely related MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism (p=0.0037). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA returned KEGG:hsa00140 (Steroid hormone biosynthesis, raw p=1.0, hit set = 5 steroids), confirming the same KEGG-level pathway. Notably, m/z-network analysis via Mummichog also captured thromboxane A2 (C02198) within the prostaglandin/arachidonic acid network (rank 2, p=0.021), a signal absent from the ORA tools because the prostaglandin pathway lacks direct annotations for thromboxane A2 in those DBs; the two-ketone/arachidonate network fragment (prostaglandin H2, E2, D2, I2, lipoxins) provides indirect connectivity evidence. Dehydroascorbic acid additionally maps to the ascorbate/aldarate metabolism network (p=0.041). Quinolinic acid appears in tryptophan/nicotinamide B3 pathways via both Mummichog and RaMP, consistent with its known role as a neuroactive tryptophan metabolite. The convergence of five steroid hormones across ORA (FDR < 10^-13) and network topology (100% pathway overlap in Mummichog) constitutes a highly robust, multi-paradigm signal indicating systemic perturbation of androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and interconversion, with secondary prostaglandin and tryptophan-axis effects.

  "narrative_text": "Three pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on steroid hormone metabolism as the dominant biological signal in the treatment-versus-control comparison. RaMP multi-database ORA returned SMPDB:SMP00068 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) at rank 1 with FDR=2.16e-14 and fold-enrichment=1250.95, driven by five steroid input metabolites — testosterone, 17β-estradiol, androstenedione, dehydroepiandrosterone, and 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one — out of five steroid inputs submitted. Reactome R-HSA-196071 (Metabolism of steroid hormones) ranked just below at FDR=1.10e-13, confirming the same signal across the Reactome namespace. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed hsa00140 with five steroid hits, establishing cross-tool consistency on androgen and estrogen biosynthesis. The m/z-direct Mummichog analysis independently recovered MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as its top hit (p=0.0018), with all five input steroids resolved within the C21-steroid module and five additional network intermediates connecting them, yielding a 10-compound module hit. The closely related MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism module ranked second (p=0.0026). Thromboxane A2 (C02198) maps to MUMM:prostaglandin_formation_from_arachidonate (rank 3, p=0.022) — a network fragment encompassing prostaglandin H2, E2, D2, I2, thromboxane B2, and lipoxins — consistent with arachidonic acid cascade involvement. Quinolinic acid (C03722) appears in MUMM:vitamin_b3_nicotinate_and_nicotinamide_metabolism (p=0.053), placing the tryptophan-derived neuroactive metabolite on the B3 axis. Dehydroascorbic acid (C05422) is annotated in MUMM:ascorbate_vitamin_c_and_aldarate_metabolism (p=0.042). Reactome R-HSA-196071 (Metabolism of steroid hormones) ranked just below at FDR=1.10e-13, confirming the same signal across the Reactome namespace.
The m/z-direct Mummichog analysis independently recovered MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as its top hit (p=0.0018).
Thromboxane A2 (C02198) maps to MUMM:prostaglandin_formation_from_arachidonate (rank 3, p=0.022) — a network fragment encompassing prostaglandin H2, E2, D2, I2, thromboxane B2, and lipoxins.
Quinolinic acid (C03722) appears in MUMM:vitamin_b3_nicotinate_and_nicotinamide_metabolism (p=0.053), placing the tryptophan-derived neuroactive metabolite on the B3 axis.
Dehydroascorbic acid (C05422) is annotated in MUMM:ascorbate_vitamin_c_and_aldarate_metabolism (p=0.042).

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on steroid hormone metabolism as the dominant biological signal in the treatment-versus-control comparison. RaMP multi-database ORA returned SMPDB:SMP00068 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) at rank 1 with FDR=2.16e-14 and fold-enrichment=1250.95, driven by five steroid input metabolites — testosterone, 17β-estradiol, androstenedione, dehydroepiandrosterone, and 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one — out of five steroid inputs submitted. Reactome R-HSA-196071 (Metabolism of steroid hormones) ranked just below at FDR=1.10e-13, confirming the same signal across the Reactome namespace. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed hsa00140 with five steroid hits, establishing cross-tool consistency on androgen and estrogen biosynthesis. The m/z-direct Mummichog analysis independently recovered MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as its top hit (p=0.0018), with all five input steroids resolved within the C21-steroid module and five additional network intermediates connecting them, yielding a 10-compound module hit. The closely related MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism module ranked second (p=0.0026). Thromboxane A2 (C02198) maps to MUMM:prostaglandin_formation_from_arachidonate (rank 3, p=0.022) — a network fragment encompassing prostaglandin H2, E2, D2, I2, thromboxane B2, and lipoxins — consistent with arachidonic acid cascade involvement. Quinolinic acid (C03722) appears in MUMM:vitamin_b3_nicotinate_and_nicotinamide_metabolism (p=0.053), placing the tryptophan-derived neuroactive metabolite on the B3 axis. Dehydroascorbic acid (C05422) is annotated in MUMM:ascorbate_vitamin_c_and_aldarate_metabolism (p=0.042). The convergence of five androgen and estrogen steroids across two complementary ORA tools and the network-topology Mummichog analysis represents a robust, multi-paradigm signal for systemic perturbation of steroid hormone biosynthesis and interconversion.
